title: FAA Approves Boeing's Biggest 737 Max Jet After Years of Delays
summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration, the U.S. agency that oversees air safety, approved Boeing's 737 Max 10 jet for passenger flights on Tuesday. The decision came nearly ten years after Boeing first showed off the plane in 2017.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy announced the approval at Boeing's factory in Everett, Washington. He said it followed extensive safety reviews, including thousands of hours of test flights, and called it a big win for American manufacturing.

The Max 10 is the largest plane in Boeing's 737 Max family. It will usually carry 185 to 210 passengers, more than the smaller Max 8 and Max 9. Airlines could use it to carry more people on one flight. Travelers might eventually see more seats on popular routes, but the effect on ticket prices will depend on how airlines use the planes.

Boeing has faced years of safety and quality problems. Two crashes of the smaller Max 8 in 2018 and 2019 led to big changes in how the FAA checks Boeing's planes. In 2024, a panel came off an Alaska Airlines Max 9 during a flight, bringing more questions about how Boeing builds its jets.

Stephanie Pope, who leads Boeing's passenger plane business, called the approval a major milestone in the company's recovery.

More than 30 customers, including United, Delta and American Airlines, have ordered 1,555 Max 10 jets. Boeing expects to start delivering them in 2027. The plane is meant to compete with the Airbus A321neo.

Approval means the design meets safety standards. Boeing must still show it can build each plane correctly, and every jet must be cleared before carrying passengers.
why_it_matters: The approval affects how many seats airlines can offer and is an important test of whether Boeing can recover after years of safety problems.
